name: Chikungunya

pathogens.why: Severe, often disabling, symmetric small-joint arthralgia accompanying fever in an Aedes-endemic area and season is the clinical hallmark of chikungunya, distinguishing it from dengue (which favors myalgia/retro-orbital pain over severe arthralgia) and from bacterial causes of joint symptoms (which are typically asymmetric/monoarticular).

investigations.why: Confirms the diagnosis; RT-PCR is most sensitive in the first few days, IgM becomes detectable slightly later.
Co-circulation with dengue is common and clinical distinction is imperfect — concurrent testing avoids missing dengue, which has different monitoring needs.
Typically shows lymphopenia rather than the thrombocytopenia more characteristic of dengue, supporting clinical distinction.

reason: Fever with severe, often symmetric, small-joint polyarthralgia (the hallmark feature distinguishing chikungunya from dengue) is consistent with chikungunya virus infection — another Aedes-transmitted viral illness. Antibiotics have no role. Management is supportive, focused on analgesia, since joint symptoms can persist for weeks to months after the acute febrile illness resolves.
